newsitem.title: UK: British producer prices unchanged in February.
newsitem.headline: British producer prices unchanged in February.

text.p: British output producer prices were unchanged in February to show a 1.3 percent year on year rise, official figures showed on Monday.
Input prices fell 0.5 percent in February for a 6.6 percent year on year fall. The figures were in line with analysts' expectations.
The Treasury said the figures were "outstanding" and meant Britain had an "unclouded" outlook for retail prices for the next few months.
Analysts said the data showed there were few inflationary pressures in the economy and meant interest rates would almost certainly remain at 6.0 percent until the election, due by May 22.

"The fall in input prices reflects the strength of sterling and maybe falling oil prices too. The critical factor now is the extent to which weak producer prices feed through into retail prices," said Philip Shaw, economist at Union Plc.
